# Synthetic speech fixtures

A small English speech dataset for testing voice data pipelines: validators, manifest readers, normalization jobs, session archives and generation workflows. It is shared by the tests in this repository and is safe to copy into other projects.

No recording of a person is used anywhere in this folder. Every clip is speech generated by a text-to-speech model from the sentences in `tools/make_fixtures.py`, and the speakers are pseudonymous ids (`spk_a`, `spk_b`) that name no one.

## Contents

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `audio/` | Eight valid clips: 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM WAV, 2.5 to 3.5 seconds each, two speakers. |
| `manifest.jsonl` | One NeMo-style line per valid clip, validated by `schemas/dataset-line.schema.json`. Each line has the clip duration, transcript, speaker, split, a consent id and the SHA-256 of the file. |
| `consents/` | One consent and license record per speaker, validated by `schemas/consent-record.schema.json`. Both are `synthetic` records: no person is recorded, so the evidence kind is `not-applicable-synthetic`. |
| `session/` | A four-turn, two-speaker session: a mixed recording, one track per speaker and `session-manifest.json`, validated by `schemas/session-manifest.schema.json`. It includes the result of the session quality and safety evaluation. |
| `audio-invalid/` | Seven deliberately invalid clips, one defect each: wrong sample rate, stereo, silent, clipped, too short, truncated and a duration that disagrees with its manifest line. |
| `invalid-manifest.jsonl` | The manifest lines that point at the invalid clips, plus one line with an empty transcript. |
| `invalid-expected.json` | The defect code each invalid line must trigger. The tests assert that each one is detected. |
| `croissant.json` | [Croissant](https://github.com/mlcommons/croissant) metadata for the valid clips and `manifest.jsonl`. |

## What the checks cover

`python tools/validate_contracts.py` and `tests/test_fixtures.py` check, for every valid line and for the session:

- the line, record or manifest against its schema;
- the clip against the audio rules in `tools/audio_checks.py`: 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM, at least 0.5 seconds, not silent, not clipped, not truncated;
- the declared `duration` against the duration in the WAV header, within one millisecond;
- the declared size and SHA-256 against the file;
- every `consent_id` against an active consent record that belongs to the same speaker and permits the use (`training` for the `train` split, `evaluation` otherwise).

`python tools/audio_checks.py FILE.wav [DURATION]` runs the audio rules on one file and prints the defect codes.

## Provenance and license

- **Voices.** Generated with Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0, https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M) through the `kokoro-onnx` package, version 0.6.1, with the voices `af_heart` (`spk_a`) and `am_michael` (`spk_b`). The model was run at 24 kHz, resampled to 16 kHz with a windowed-sinc filter and peak-normalized to 80 percent of full scale.
- **Text.** Short sentences written for these fixtures. They name no person, organization or product.
- **Generation.** Run `tools/make_fixtures.py`; it needs the packages in `requirements-fixtures.txt` and the model files, which are not committed:

  ```bash
  python -m venv .venv-fixtures
  .venv-fixtures/bin/pip install -r requirements-fixtures.txt
  mkdir -p .kokoro-models
  # Download kokoro-v1.0.onnx and voices-v1.0.bin from
  # https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases/tag/model-files-v1.0
  # into .kokoro-models/, then:
  .venv-fixtures/bin/python tools/make_fixtures.py
  ```

  The files used for the committed audio have these SHA-256 values:

  ```text
  7d5df8ecf7d4b1878015a32686053fd0eebe2bc377234608764cc0ef3636a6c5  kokoro-v1.0.onnx
  bca610b8308e8d99f32e6fe4197e7ec01679264efed0cac9140fe9c29f1fbf7d  voices-v1.0.bin
  ```

  Speech synthesis can differ slightly between platforms and library versions, so a rebuild may change the audio bytes. The fixtures are committed so that tests and CI read them as they are and never run the model. Regenerating rewrites every generated file in this folder and keeps this README.
- **License.** The fixtures are released under the MIT license of this repository, copyright Backblaze, Inc. The Kokoro-82M model is Apache-2.0 and is not part of this repository.
- **Fixed values.** Timestamps in the manifests are fixed constants so that a rebuild produces the same text.

## Using the fixtures from another project

Copy this folder and `schemas/`, or pin the repository at a tag and read the files from it. Keep `manifest.jsonl`, `consents/` and `session/` together: the manifests refer to each other by id and by relative path.
